newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says France's concerns have been understood.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says France's concerns have been understood.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Thursday that his new Socialist government's concerns on Europe had been understood.

He was speaking after a meeting with European Commission President Jacques Santer, who is seeking a compromise to resolve a row over the EU's "stability pact" limiting budget deficits of countries that join a single European currency.

"I think the preoccupations we are expressing do not simply concern France. They concern the whole of Europe," Jospin told reporters. "Therefore I think these concerns have been understood. We are making progress."

Santer said both he and Jospin wanted to make next week's European Union summit in Amsterdam a success. The French government has not yet said whether it will back the stability pact, agreed last year and due to have been approved by EU leaders in Amsterdam.
"We very much want the Amsterdam summit to succeed, I think that is also the wish of the prime minister," Santer said.
